title: Three Consecutive India T20I Captains Stood Together at Wankhede on Saturday. None of Them Was Angry.
excerpt: Hours after being stripped of the captaincy and dropped entirely, Suryakumar Yadav hugged Shreyas Iyer, congratulated him, and called it a proud moment for Mumbai cricket. Rohit Sharma stood beside them both.
body:
Hours after the BCCI stripped him of the captaincy and dropped him from the squad entirely, Suryakumar Yadav walked out for the toss at Wankhede Stadium on Saturday evening, looked into the camera, and said he was "very, very, very happy" for the man who replaced him.

The setting was the T20 Mumbai League. Suryakumar was captaining Triumph Knights MNE. Shreyas Iyer, India's newly appointed T20I captain, was playing for SoBo Mumbai Falcons as an Impact Substitute. Before the match began, the two shared a hug on the same ground where both had learned the game. Then Rohit Sharma, who retired from T20Is after winning the 2024 World Cup, joined them.

Three consecutive India T20I captains. All from Mumbai. All at Wankhede on the same evening, on the day the captaincy changed hands.

## What Suryakumar Actually Said

Speaking at the toss, Suryakumar chose to frame the moment not as a loss but as a point of civic pride. "Very happy for Shreyas Iyer. We played a lot of cricket for Mumbai and India together," he said. "Most importantly, three back-to-back T20I captains for India from Mumbai now. It's a very proud moment, and everyone needs to celebrate that."

The remarks were his first public response to the BCCI's announcement. They carried no trace of bitterness. He also took to Instagram, sharing the squad photo for the England tour with a message: "Wishing this highly skilled group all the best for the challenges ahead." He separately congratulated 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on his maiden India call-up.

## The Numbers Behind the Axe

The decision to remove Suryakumar was not impulsive. His form had been declining for months. During IPL 2026, he managed just 270 runs in 13 innings at an average of 20.76 for Mumbai Indians. Even during the T20 World Cup earlier this year — which India won under his leadership — his personal output was relatively quiet: 242 runs in nine innings at a strike rate of 136.72.

But Suryakumar had done something no Indian T20I captain had done before: he successfully defended the World Cup title, making India the first team to win back-to-back T20 World Cups. That achievement made his removal all the more jarring for fans.

The BCCI paid tribute on its official Instagram page, writing: "A sterling example in leadership. It was a truly memorable tenure for Surya Kumar Yadav as Team India's T20I captain that culminated into a historic ICC Men's T20 World Cup victory."

## Rohit's Endorsement of Shreyas

Rohit Sharma, who has watched both men grow through Mumbai's cricket system, was characteristically direct about the transition. "Looking at how Shreyas has captained, he's going to have a good time as India skipper," Rohit said at the event.

Shreyas Iyer's credentials are well established. He led Kolkata Knight Riders to the IPL title in 2024 and had a strong run as KKR captain in subsequent seasons. His return to the T20I setup is remarkable in itself — he has not played a T20I for India since December 2023. But the selectors, led by Ajit Agarkar, have clearly decided that his captaincy instincts and tactical nous outweigh the gap in international match time.

Iyer's immediate assignments include two T20Is in Ireland in late June, a five-match T20I series in England in July, and the Asian Games in September. He will be assisted by Tilak Varma as vice-captain.

## Five World Cup Winners Left Behind

The squad overhaul extended well beyond Suryakumar. Five members of India's victorious 2026 T20 World Cup squad were omitted from the Ireland and England selections: Suryakumar Yadav, Rinku Singh, Kuldeep Yadav, Jasprit Bumrah (rested for workload management), and Hardik Pandya (rested ahead of ODI commitments).

The changes signal a decisive pivot towards the 2028 T20 World Cup cycle. Younger players have been given the runway. The message from the selectors is unmistakable: trophies earn respect, not permanence.

## The Mumbai Factor

What made Saturday at Wankhede unusual was not the captaincy change itself — Indian cricket has seen plenty of those. It was the visual. Three men who had each led India in T20Is, standing together on a municipal cricket ground in south Mumbai, united by the city's cricket ecosystem rather than divided by the board's decisions.

Mumbai has produced Indian cricket captains for decades, from Sunil Gavaskar and Sachin Tendulkar to Rohit Sharma. But three consecutive T20I captains from the same city is a first. The MCA's president, Ajinkya Naik, was also present, and the moment was widely shared on social media.

For Suryakumar, the evening ended with a blazing 48 for Triumph Knights at Wankhede. For Shreyas, it began with a new national mandate. For Rohit, it was a chance to pass the torch he had once carried himself.

The T20 Mumbai League runs until June 13. Indian cricket's next chapter starts in Ireland later this month.
